turns.response_html:
Gestalt refers to a 1920s school of German psychology, notably led by Max Wertheimer, Kurt Koffka, and Wolfgang Köhler. They proposed that the human mind perceives objects as entire configurations rather than a mere sum of individual parts.

Core Principles

  • Emergence: You see the whole form before the individual components.
  • Reification: The mind fills in gaps to create a complete shape.
  • Multistability: The ability to toggle between two different interpretations of the same image.
  • Invariance: Recognizing objects regardless of their rotation, scale, or translation.

Key Laws of Organization

LawDescription
ProximityElements close to each other are perceived as a group.
SimilaritySimilar items are seen as being related.
ClosureThe brain automatically closes gaps in a partial image to see a whole.
ContinuityThe eye follows the smoothest path when viewing lines.
